welcome.pyMissing:
Python (py launcher) not found.
A Windows Python install is required to create profiles.
[Install Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/)
[Set py path](command:frivenv.configureProfileTools)
[Re-check](command:frivenv.recheckEnv)
welcome.noProfiles:
No profiles yet.
A profile is one virtualenv with pinned Python / frida / frida-tools versions.
[New profile](command:frivenv.newProfile)
welcome.adbMissing:
adb not found.
Android platform tools (adb) are required to work with Android devices.
[Download platform tools](https://developer.android.com/tools/releases/platform-tools)
[Set adb path](command:frivenv.configureDeviceTools)
[Re-check](command:frivenv.recheckEnv)
welcome.noDevices:
No Android devices registered.
Enable USB debugging, connect the device, then register it in the manage window.
[Open Android device manager](command:frivenv.manageDevices)
welcome.noIosDevices:
No iOS devices registered.
Add one with its SSH connection info in the manage window.
[Open iOS device manager](command:frivenv.manageIosDevices)
config.language.description: UI language. "auto" follows the VS Code display language.
config.dataDir.description: Folder for the profile/device lists and virtualenvs. Empty = the storage VS Code assigns to this extension.
config.scriptsDir.description: Folder a profile terminal starts in, so `frida -l hook.js` takes a short relative path. Empty = the open workspace folder, or the extension's `scripts` folder when no folder is open.
config.adbPath.description: Path to the adb executable. Empty = look it up on PATH.
config.pythonLauncherPath.description: Path to the py launcher. Empty = use py on PATH.
config.showInExplorer.description: Show Profiles / Android / iOS under one Frivenv section in the Explorer (on by default). Turn off to use only the Frivenv activity-bar view.
config.iosFridaServerDir.description: Default device folder for frida-server on iOS. Empty = auto: the folder the running frida-server is in, else `/var/jb/usr/sbin` on rootless jailbreaks, else `/usr/sbin`. A per-device folder set in the iOS window wins over this.
